missionPremise: Today a caller can look up A PARCEL and cannot ask a question ACROSS parcels. P-106 adds the second thing as a PROJECTION over facets that are already baked, not a pipeline. Source: _inbox/2026-09-01_p106_constraint_search_WDLL.md, operator go 2026-09-01, OPS-16 amendment A-071.
completionPredicate: A land buyer can express a constraint over one Central Texas county and get back three sets - matched, excluded, and not-evaluated with the rail named - from a cache that declares when it was built, with every refusal declared rather than errored, and can push the matched ids onto a screen with no re-fetch. Every check shown failing on a deliberate violation and passing on restore.
scopeBasis: Serve path only, in legacy-design-tools. No acquisition path, no facet re-derivation, no second store for a subject that already has one. Six Central Texas counties, because landing_parcel_jurisdiction covers 981,405 of roughly 7.6M Texas parcels and a statewide answer would imply coverage that does not exist. The DDL is written and HANDED BACK UNAPPLIED, per the dispatch, the way P-100 handed back 0093.

designDecisions.decision: The projection stores a VALUE and a STATE per rail, and the state is NOT NULL with a CHECK constraint.
designDecisions.why: A null value cannot say why it is null, and the three reasons are three different facts. The state column is what makes the three-set result expressible at all.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: A writer that skips the TypeScript (raw connection, backfill, psql) could smuggle a value under an unmeasured state. Answered in DDL: `(value IS NOT NULL) = (state = 'present')` per rail, both directions, verified by violation.

designDecisions.decision: The five state words are imported from smartSiteStub.SMART_SITE_RAIL_STATES, not retyped.
designDecisions.why: One vocabulary. get_smart_site and the projection cannot disagree about what `present` means.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: lib/db cannot import from artifacts, so the DDL's word list is a second implementation of one rule - the CTRL-1 shape. Answered with a divergence test that parses the exported SQL fragment and asserts it equals SMART_SITE_RAIL_STATES.

designDecisions.decision: EXCLUDED beats NOT-EVALUATED in the verdict precedence.
designDecisions.why: A one-acre parcel with no flood determination, asked for two acres and dry, fails on acreage whatever flood turns out to be. Calling it not-evaluated overstates the uncertainty as badly as the reverse understates it.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: The alternative (not-evaluated wins) was considered and rejected; both orderings are pinned by the nine-row real-Postgres partition fixture, so the choice is visible rather than implicit.

designDecisions.decision: The unmeasured share is computed in the SAME statement as the answer.
designDecisions.why: A separate coverage table is a mechanism somebody has to remember to refresh, and a refusal quoting a stale number is worse than no refusal.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: Costs one extra aggregate over rows already scanned. Reported on SUCCESS too (unmeasuredPctByRail), so a result that passed the gate still shows the coverage it rests on.

designDecisions.decision: The unmeasured-refusal threshold has NO DEFAULT. Unset means no gate, and the coverage is still reported.
designDecisions.why: The card states the threshold is an operator ruling. A default would be the silently-picked number the card forbids, and it would be invisible in every response.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: This means the gate is dormant until the operator rules. That is stated here rather than papered over with a plausible number, and unmeasuredPctByRail on every success is what keeps the absence of a gate from hiding anything.

designDecisions.decision: Every declared refusal is a 422 serve_refused body in the SAME envelope radius-search and street-search already use.
designDecisions.why: declarePlaceSearchRefusal in the MCP package reads that envelope already. A second refusal shape would be two implementations of one rule.
designDecisions.adversarialCheck: constraint_rail_unmeasured must carry a NUMBER, and gtmErrorBody spreads extras at the top level where the MCP mapper would drop them. Answered by nesting the evidence under `detail` and teaching the mapper to pass `detail` through verbatim.

threeQuestionGate.control: The projection's value/state invariant and the closed rail-state vocabulary
threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesIt: Postgres CHECK constraints created by migration 0094 and by the drizzle schema (both, identically - proven by a constraint-definition diff)
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: Every INSERT or UPDATE on pe_parcel_constraint_index, from any client, including a raw psql session
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenViolated: The write is refused with a named constraint. Shown: 8 deliberate violations, 8 refusals, 3 corrected rows accepted, exactly 3 rows admitted.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: Nothing that writes through Postgres. It IS bypassed by: (1) the migration never being applied - this lane hands it back unapplied by instruction, so the control is written and NOT ARMED IN PRODUCTION today, and that is stated rather than implied; (2) a future ALTER TABLE dropping a constraint, which the constraint-definition diff against migration 0094 would catch only if somebody runs it.
